title: Product-key cell-granularity diagnostic for fixed-K persistent-state retrieval
question: Does increasing product-key factor granularity reduce the fraction of persistent states subjected to teacher reranking while preserving the retrieval behavior of the fixed exhaustive reference?
hypothesis: The fixed factor-size-8 product-key index scores a roughly constant fraction of the state population because its 64-cell topology becomes increasingly occupied. Increasing factor size should reduce state occupancy per selected cell union and therefore reduce states scored per M, subject to a possible coverage tradeoff.

arms.name: factor_size_8
arms.intervention: two-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8

arms.name: factor_size_16
arms.intervention: two-factor product-key addressing with factor size 16

arms.name: factor_size_32
arms.intervention: two-factor product-key addressing with factor size 32

decision_rule.condition: report target recall, proposal retention, states scored/M, shortlist size, nonempty cells, and arithmetic separately for factor sizes 8,16,32 at each M
decision_rule.licenses: diagnostic evidence about product-key cell granularity on the registered workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal product-key retrieval guarantees, universal sublinear scaling, or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: a larger factor size materially lowers states scored/M while retrieval remains close to the exhaustive reference
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support that fixed-factor collision/occupancy is a principal limitation of the current product-key construction
decision_rule.does_not_license: general semantic addressing or a broad C5 capability claim

held_constant: same 48 training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
same task seed stream across arms
